_why: GraphCode's envelope parser and block scanner exist twice: GraphCodeSidecarReader.cpp, which
the save hook, GcCheck and gc_apply use, and gc-sidecar.js, which is what lets gc_read answer
with the editor closed. Two implementations of a grammar is how a language drifts. Neither of
these understands a STATEMENT - both only split named blocks and hand the bytes on - but the
split itself still has to agree, byte for byte, or a block edited through one and applied
through the other is a half-applied asset rather than a parse error.
So both suites assert against this file. A change to either scanner that moves a boundary
fails on both sides at once, which is the only arrangement in which 'they agree' is a fact
rather than a hope.
The fixtures deliberately carry the cases that break a naive brace counter: a designer label
whose text is '{ not a block }', a backtick identifier ending in '}', an '# UNSUPPORTED:'
note containing '}', and nested braces three deep.
legacy_flat_struct.gc is the other shape entirely: a flat body with no blocks at all and an
ir: token no current build emits. NOTHING PROJECTS LIKE THIS ANY MORE - a user struct now
writes schemacode/1 blocks - and that is exactly why it is kept. A reader that only handles
what today's writer emits cannot read a repository's own history, and these files are
committed, so history is the normal case. Both scanners drive the block/no-block decision off
the TEXT rather than off the asset kind, which is what makes one scanner honest for both.
sig: is NOT part of this contract. It is BLAKE3 over the body and the JS side has no BLAKE3,
so it carries the token instead of checking it. What both sides do promise is the envelope
fields and the block split, and that is what is written down here.
A LABELLED BLOCK: `behaviortree BTGraph  sig:<digest> {` — three tokens before the brace,
where every other block is one. GraphCodeSidecarReader.cpp learned this shape on 2026-08-18
and gc-sidecar.js had not, so the bridge refused every behavior tree and every EQS query with
"Expected a block name before '{' ... found 'sig:...'" — on gc_read's DEFAULT saved source.
Neither existing fixture labels a block, which is why the shared suite could not see it.
It also carries `blackboard:` and `baseline:`, two of the four envelope lines the JS parser
refused outright until the same day. 92 of this project's 407 sidecars state `baseline:`.
